text_blocks.snippet: According to the American Heart Association, high blood pressure (hypertension) is defined as a reading of 130/80 mm Hg or higher.
Blood pressure is written as two numbers:

list.snippet: Systolic (top number): The force when your heart beats.
Diastolic (bottom number): The force when your heart rests between beats.
Normal: Less than 120/80 mm Hg (top number is under 120 AND bottom number is under 80).
Elevated: 120–129 systolic AND less than 80 diastolic.
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 or higher systolic OR 90 or higher diastolic.
Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 for the top number and/or higher than 120 for the bottom number. (Seek emergency medical care immediately.)

text_blocks.snippet: You only need one of the numbers (top or bottom) to be high to fall into a higher category.
If you'd like, you can share:

list.snippet: Whether you were resting when you took them

text_blocks.snippet: I can help you understand which category they fall into.
